title: Pedro Clerot: My Ultimate Driver
excerpt:
Pedro Clerot’s preparations for the 2027 campaign have begun with the Rodin Motorsport driver having taken part in the Jerez post-season test earlier this week.

Recently, we caught up with the Brazilian to build his ultimate racing driver, and there are a few motorsport legends on Clerot’s list.

INTELLIGENCE

“That's a really good question. I'm going to say Senna. From everything I've seen from Ayrton, from his days, he was a guy that was always ahead of his time on and off track, so that's one of the big reasons why.

DRIVING IN THE WET

“Senna again. I think it's pretty straightforward. What Ayrton did in the wet was always spectacular, so I have to go with him.”

The Brazilian earmarked Ayrton Senna for his intelligence and ability in the wet

The Rodin driver picked out Norris for his smooth driving stule

SMOOTH DRIVING STYLE

“Smoothest, I'm going to say, it's difficult actually, it can be a tricky question. The smoothest driving style, I'd say Lando. He drives really clean all the time, but Oscar also does. I'll go with Lando.”

AGGRESSIVE DRIVING STYLE

“I guess this is back to Max.”

ANYTHING ELSE?

“I would put Nelson Piquet’s technical knowledge, for sure. That guy is unbelievable. We live quite close in Brasilia, and I've been lucky enough to have a few chats with him while go-karting and also sometimes having dinner with him, so his technical knowledge is unreal, so it's a good mention to put that.”

title: Freddie Slater set for F1 race weekend debut with Audi in Mexico City and Sao Paulo
excerpt:
Freddie Slater will make his debut on a Formula 1 race weekend with the Audi Formula 1 Team, taking part in both the Mexico City and Sao Paulo Grands Prix Free Practice 1 sessions.

Slater had a strong season in Formula 3, fighting for the title until the final round. He finished second in the Championship with eight podiums, including a Feature Race victory in Budapest with TRIDENT.

For 2027, the 18-year-old is set to step up to FIA Formula 2 with Invicta Racing.

Before then, Slater will make his debut in F1 for Audi in Mexico, before driving in FP1 again a week later in Sao Paulo.

At the announcement, the British driver expressed how excited he was to achieve a childhood dream.

“Getting behind the wheel of a Formula One car at a Grand Prix weekend is a big moment for me and something I’ve been dreaming of since I was a kid,” said Slater. “I’ve learned a lot this year, and these Free Practice outings with Audi Revolut F1 Team will be another opportunity to keep gaining on-track experience.

“Being part of the Audi Driver Development Programme has already given me some incredible opportunities, and I am grateful for their trust and support. I’m really looking forward to getting out on track: m y focus will be on doing the best job I can, helping the team with its programme and taking as many learnings as possible from both sessions.”

Racing Director and Director of the Audi Development Programme, Allan McNish added: “We have seen Freddie making great progress throughout recent years, both on and off the track; it is the right time for Freddie to step-up. These appearances in Mexico and Brazil will give him valuable experience of a Formula One race weekend, and another chance to continue his development before he steps up to Formula 2 next season. We are looking forward to seeing him in the R26 and supporting him through these two important FP1 sessions.”

title: ‘I had a blast’ - Macedo pleased with performance after ‘unexpected’ test with VAR in Jerez
excerpt:
Francisco Macedo set the fastest time of this week’s Jerez post-season test, after receiving a late call up from Van Amersfoort Racing.

The Portuguese driver showed strong pace, recovering from some issues on Day 1 to top the timesheets on the second day’s morning session.

When times were at their quickest during the qualifying runs, Macedo completed a 1:29.766, the best time of the week, leading fellow VAR driver Enzo Deligny by 0.169s.

Macedo followed that up with a run to second in the afternoon, which was dominated by race simulations.

Speaking in the paddock at the end of the test, Macedo reflected on the unexpected opportunity to jump into the F3 car.

“It was a bit of an unexpected test,” he said. “I actually received a late call. I tried to prepare myself as best as possible, and today I managed to get a P1 in the morning, P2 in the afternoon.

Macedo set the fastest time of the test ahead of fellow VAR driver Deligny

“Unfortunately, yesterday I had some issues during the day, but me and the team managed to solve them during the night, and today we were fastest.”

Speaking further about his time driving the Formula 3 car, Macedo picked out the best parts of the experience.

AS IT HAPPENED: Follow all the action from Day 2 of post-season testing in Jerez

Nakamura-Berta reflects on ‘big learning day’ after ending up fastest in Jerez

“It was my first time in the F3, and it's completely different to the FREC that I am used to driving,” he explained.

“It has a lot more speed, a lot better braking, and I just had a blast. VAR was my team from last year, so it was quite easy to adapt to that aspect.

“I already knew everyone and I felt very comfortable since day one with the team and of course with the car too.”

Macedo talked about adapting to the Formula 3 car and how much he enjoyed the experience

Speaking more about the challenges that he had to adapt to, Macedo picked out tyre management on race runs, especially with there being two different compounds this week – the Medium and the Hard.

“It was a big challenge because in my previous categories, it was always a one-compound tyre,” he explained.

Nakamura-Berta ends Day 1 of Jerez post-season testing on top

PREVIEW: 2026 Post-Season Testing starts with two days in Jerez

“So here we had two compounds and also the tyre life is a lot shorter. I had to be a lot more on it from the first lap.

“Then also the race runs were a bit more tricky, with more tyre degradation. I just had to adapt and learn as much as possible.

When asked if he had adapted well to the tyres by the end, Macedo joked: “Actually I managed to survive at least to the end.”

title: Francisco Macedo fastest on Day 2 of Jerez Post-Season test for Van Amersfoort Racing
excerpt:
Francisco Macedo ended Day 2 of post-season testing in Jerez with the fastest time of the test for Van Amersfoort Racing.

The Portuguese driver was quickest during the morning’s qualifying simulations on a 1:29.766, with Rodin Motorsport’s Alessandro Giusti on top in the afternoon session with a 1:30.322.

MORNING

After a brief Red Flag caused by an issue for Alessandro Giusti, Pedro Clerot took to the top with a 1:31.659.

But the Red Flags were waved once again with Alexander Abkhazava in the gravel at Turn 3.

Once the action resumed, Ernesto Rivera went to P1 on a 1:31.584. But there were several more improvements to come, with Taito Kato leading Keanu Al Ahzari by 0.003s with a 1:31.463.

Dion Gowda then went fastest with a 1:30.935 before improving to a 1:30.860, putting 0.169s between he and teammate James Egozi.

Al Azhari briefly went top with a 1:30.700, before Mattia Colnaghi eclipsed that time by 0.029s.

Kato was flying and completed an eye-catching 1:30.386 to put 0.266s between he and Rivera.

Niccolò Maccagnani then lowered the time to beat to a 1:30.302 with just over 90 minutes to go in the session.

Moments later, the Red Flags were waved with Francisco Macedo having stopped on track at Turn 8. But once the action resumed Colnaghi retook his place at the top with a 1:30.037.

The Argentinian driver was over two-and-a half tenths clear of the rest, although Jin Nakamura reduced the gap to 0.136s.

As the second hour of running came to an end, Enzo Deligny became the first to go into the 1:29s. The Van Amersfoort Racing driver’s 1:29.935 put him on top by 0.017s to Clerot. Macedo then made it a VAR 1-2, going fastest on a 1:29.766.

Into the final hour, and race runs were the focus for the majority, although with 30 minutes to go, there was a Red Flag. Maciej Gladysz found the gravel at Turn 5.

Running resumed, but there were no further changes to the timesheets, leaving Macedo on top ahead of Deligny, Clerot, Reza Seewooruthun, and Colnaghi.

AFTERNOON

After missing most of the morning session, Giusti returned to the track in the afternoon, and completed a 1:30.322 to lead the way.

Long runs were the focus for the teams after that, although there was a stoppage with just under two hours to go with Miguel Costa having stopped at the pit entry.

Once the lights turned green, practice starts and race simulations were still on the agenda, meaning there were no improvements to the timesheets.

Giusti ended up on top ahead of Macedo, Nakamura, Alex Powell and Nandhavud Bhirombhakdi.

That wraps up the Jerez post-season test but the drivers will be back out on track in Barcelona from October 26-27.

title: Nakamura-Berta reflects on ‘big learning day’ after ending up fastest in Jerez
excerpt:
Kean Nakamura-Berta was happy with how things went on the opening day of running in Jerez

Kean Nakamura-Berta hailed a productive opening day of post-season testing in Jerez, with the TRIDENT driver ending up at the top of the leaderboard.

The British rookie showed good pace throughout the day before going to the top of the timesheets late in the afternoon session.

Nakamura-Berta’s 1:31.169 put him on top by 0.002s to Campos Racing’s Mattia Colnaghi, with Ernesto Rivera rounding out the top three – 0.011s off the leading time.

Speaking in the paddock after debriefing with the team, Nakamura-Berta reflected on a positive day of running in Jerez.

“Overall it was a very productive day,” he said. “We were learning loads of new stuff with this new car, and obviously the jump to F3 is massive, so it's just been a big learning day.

“Obviously tomorrow will be as well, and so will Barcelona next week. But it's been really, really fun to drive around here.

Nakamura-Berta was happy with a productive first day of running in Formula 3

“The track is insane, it's super fun, and it's challenging in parts, heavy braking, high speed as well. So it's really good to develop and then understand how to drive the car.

“Everyone's testing different things and different run plans, but I think it's been positive. The pace definitely doesn't look too shabby. But there's loads to improve on and work on as well, so we just keep going forwards.”

AS IT HAPPENED: Follow the action on Day 1 of post-season testing in Jerez

PREVIEW: 2026 Post-Season Testing starts with two days in Jerez

When asked what his takeaways were about the Formula 3 car after one day of running, Nakamura-Berta spoke about the different things he has to learn and adapt too.

“One lap on the peak to get the tyre into that working optimal temperature is quite difficult,” he explained. “That's been a key thing for me, at least today.

“I really struggled the majority of the day to do it, and towards the end we started to find a good rhythm. But I definitely still need to work on a lot of things to improve and work on.

Nakamura-Berta was happy with how he and TRIDENT worked together on Day 1

“But it's been a really solid first day. The team have been incredible, and we have worked really well, so we just keep going.”

Looking ahead to Day 2 in Jerez, Nakamura-Berta and TRIDENT still have a few tyres remaining, and while chasing fast times is fun, he says the focus will remain on improving further in the car.

“We have tyres left, we have Mediums left, we also have Hards left,” said Nakamura-Berta. “So we'll just keep on our plan, we'll just keep working within ourselves internally.

“We’ve got incredible data from the past, loads of really strong drivers have come through this team, so we've got good data there to compare too.

“So that's what we'll just be comparing to, and we will just have a little glance at the timesheets once in a while, but it’s mainly about working inside and just trying to learn as much as possible before the season starts.”

title: Nakamura-Berta ends Day 1 of Jerez post-season testing on top
excerpt:
Kean Nakamura-Berta ended Day 1 of the Jerez post-season test on top for TRIDENT.

The British driver completed a 1:31.169 in the afternoon session to top the times, with Campos Racing’s Ernesto Rivera having led the way in the morning with a 1:31.217.

MORNING

It was a quiet first part of the day as installation laps took priority with the drivers and teams looking to get everything in order before hitting the track for their flying laps.

As the first 90 minutes of the day came to an end, AIX Racing sent their three drivers out for the flying laps of the day.

James Egozi completed a 1:34.526 before improving to a 1:32.680 on his next attempt. On each occasion, he was over seven-tenths quicker than teammate Dion Gowda.

MP Motorsport’s Matteo De Palo then beat that time with a 1:32.353. The Italian clocked a 1:31.867 on his next lap, with Maciej Gladysz going to P2 – 0.582s down on his teammate.

Hitech’s Kanato Le cut the gap down to De Palo to just 0.105s with DAMS Lucas Oil’s Miguel Costa going up to P3.

On his next lap, Costa took over at the top by 0.038s, completing a 1:31.829 to cap a solid start to the test.

Teams’ champions Campos Racing then made their first move of the day, as Ernesto Rivera went quickest on a 1:31.217 on a new set of Mediums. Teammate Mattia Colnaghi was second, over three-tenths behind.

With 15 minutes left in the session, Enzo Deligny moved up to P2, 0.188s down on Rivera.

There were no further improvements in the session, with Rivera remaining on top ahead of Deligny, Colnaghi, Alessandro Giusti and Alexander Abkhazava.

AFTERNOON

Rivera picked up where he left off in the morning to set the fastest time of a 1:31.784. However, he was quickly demoted to P2 by TRIDENT’s Niccolò Maccagnani on a 1:31.632.

Long runs then became the focus for the teams, although we did see a few improvements as Rashid Al Dhaheri went up to fourth ahead of Taito Kato.

Costa continued his fine form with DAMS by going up to third with just over 45 minutes left in the session, 0.293s away from Maccagnani.

As the session approached its final stages, a few teams put on a set of new Hard tyres, and with that Kean Nakamura-Berta went top on a 1:31.169.

Maccagnani followed him across the line moments later to go up to P2, making it a TRIDENT 1-2, with the Italian driver just 0.044s away from his teammate.

Colnaghi then made a late move up the leaderboard for Campos, going to within 0.002s off Nakamura-Berta, with Rivera in P3, just 0.011s away from the leading time.

Heading into the final few minutes, DAMS Lucas Oil’s Abkhazava, stopped on track, with the session unable to start before the chequered flag was waved.

That wraps up Day 1 in Jerez, with Nakamura-Berta on top ahead of Colnaghi, Rivera, Maccagnani and Giusti. Egozi was sixth, ahead of Taito Kato, De Palo, Sebastian Wheldon, and Emmanuele Olivieri.

The drivers will be back out on track for the final day of testing in Jerez at 09:00 local time tomorrow morning.

title: MP Motorsport confirm the signing of Zhenrui Chi for the 2027 season
excerpt:
MP Motorsport have confirmed the signing of Zhenrui Chi for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season.

Chi made the step up to single seater racing in 2024, finishing fifth in the Formula Trophy UAE after a strong karting career.

In 2025, the Aston Martin Driver Academy member achieved one win and four podiums in total in the Italian F4 Championship, ending up fifth in the Drivers’ Standings.

Chi will now graduate to Formula 3 with MP having raced for them in this year’s Formula Regional European Championship where he finished eighth.

The 17-year-old will now race alongside Matteo De Palo and Maciej Gladysz at MP and he expressed his excitement at getting to continue with the Dutch team.

“I am truly delighted with my promotion to Formula 3, especially while doing so with MP Motorsport”, said Chi. “We have gelled really well in the FIA Formula Regional European Championship this season, so my confidence is high for a repeat.

“The team have done really well in F3 this year, certainly towards the end of the season, so it’s my goal to contribute to the team’s ultimate pace and have their outstanding form last well into next season.”

MP Motorsport’s Team Principal Sander Dorsman also added: “We are very happy to retain Newman for his step up to FIA Formula 3. In FIA FREC this year, he has seldomly put a foot wrong, demonstrating his ability to be a consistent front-runner, which is absolutely what you need in a highly competitive environment such as FIA F3. With Maciej, Matteo and Newman, we have an exciting mix of experience and youthful energy that will hold us in good stead for 2027.”

title: Mattia Colnaghi joins Campos Racing for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Campos Racing have confirmed the signing of Mattia Colnaghi for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season.

Colnaghi returns for a second campaign in F3 after a positive rookie year where he finished 13th in the Standings with 54 points.

The 18-year-old boasts a strong record in single seater racing having won the 2024 Spanish F4 title and the 2025 Eurocup-3 championship.

Colnaghi is now set to move to Campos for another season in Formula 3, and at the announcement, he expressed his excitement at joining the reigning Driver and Teams’ champions.

"Very happy to join forces with Campos Racing for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season," said Colnaghi. "Having raced against the team in previous categories, I’ve always had great respect for them and the success they’ve achieved across the feeder series, especially in F3 as reigning Team and Drivers’ Champions.

"After winning championships in previous categories and gaining a year of valuable experience in F3, I believe that together with Campos, we have the potential to fight for big results in 2027. Excited to get to work during post-season testing and build towards a great season."

Team Principal Adrián Campos added: “We are very proud to welcome Mattia to our FIA Formula 3 driver line-up for 2027. He is an extremely talented driver and has shown his ability to fight for wins and championships from his very first steps in single-seaters.

"We will work with him throughout the winter to make sure we are as well prepared as possible for what will be a very demanding season. After the results we have achieved over the past two years, our goal is to continue fighting at the front and defend the titles we have secured this year. We are confident that Mattia has everything it takes to help us achieve that.”

title: Maciej Gladysz moves to MP Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
MP Motorsport have announced that Maciej Gladysz will race for the team in the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season.

Gladysz returns for a second campaign in F3 after a strong rookie year where he achieved a Feature Race victory at Silverstone, and finishing 12th in the Drivers’ Standings.

The Polish driver started with MP for his first two years in the single seater racing, finishing third in both 2024 editions of the Formula Winter Series and Spanish F4 Championship.

In 2025, Gladysz and MP won the Eurocup-3 Spanish Winter Championship.

Looking ahead to 2027, Gladysz is excited to be reunited with the Dutch team.

“I’m extremely pleased to rejoin the MP family for my second go at FIA F3”, said Gładysz. “I have happy memories of my years with the team, especially my debut season in single-seaters in which I became a race winner in only my third weekend.

“MP have come up very strong in the final part of the F3 season to clinch third in the teams standings, and with a year’s experience under my belt, it’s my goal to help the team transform that run of form into more wins in 2027. I can’t wait to get started!”

MP Motorsport Team Principal Sander Dorsman also added: “It’s an absolute joy to welcome Maciej back into the fold. We recorded six race wins and 16 podiums in the two seasons we spent together, and I see no reason why we shouldn’t add any more to those. Maciej has been truly outstanding on his FIA F3 debut and for many in the team, he is a known quantity, which will help us hit the ground running in our preparation for the new season.”

title: Niccolò Maccagnani signs with TRIDENT for the 2027 season
excerpt:
TRIDENT have signed Niccolò Maccagnani for the 2027 season – completing their lineup for the upcoming campaign following the announcements of Kean Nakamura-Berta and Sebastian Wheldon.

Maccagnani made the step up to single seaters in 2025 and finished second in the Formula Trophy. In 2026, the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy member finished fourth in the UAE4 Series with two victories and five podiums in total.

Maccagnani has also achieved two victories in this year’s Italian F4 Championship and took part in the final round of the Formula 3 season in Madrid.

The 16-year-old will now step up to F3 full time with TRIDENT and Team Manager Giacomo Ricci is delighted to have him onboard for 2027.

“We are delighted to announce the arrival of Niccolò Maccagnani at TRIDENT Motorsport," said Ricci. "Niccolò is a young driver who has already demonstrated his speed and potential, excelling in the junior formulae.

"The FIA Formula 3 Championship will represent a significant challenge, with cars and a competitiveness level that are higher than anything he has faced so far. We are ready to provide Niccolò with full support in this new phase of his career, working together to foster his growth and allow him to fully express his talents and perform a competitive season.”

title: Dion Gowda completes LN4 Fusion lineup for the 2027 season
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion have finalised their driver lineup for the 2027 season with Dion Gowda set to join the team for the upcoming campaign.

Gowda stepped up to single seater racing in 2023 and finished fourth in the British F4 Championship with four victories and six podiums in total.

Most recently, the 18-year-old spent two seasons in the Formula Regional European Championship, achieving several points finishes across both campaigns.

The Indian driver is now set to race alongside James Egozi and Gabriel Gomez at the team in 2027, and he expressed his delight at joining LN4 for this next step in his career.

“I'm really excited to be joining LN4 Fusion for the FIA Formula 3 Championship next year," said Gowda. "Racing in FIA F3 is a dream come true and I'm really grateful for the opportunity. There are amazing people in this team, and I can’t wait to get started!”

LN4 Fusion Chief Executive Officer Dan Richards added: "We are delighted to welcome Dion to LN4 Fusion, and we are very happy to be working with him. He showed promising speed in Formula Regional this season, regularly running in the top 10. We believe there is plenty of room for him to keep growing as a competitor, and on top of that he is a great person to work with. Everyone in the team is looking forward to starting this new journey together."

title: Matteo De Palo returns with MP Motorsport for the 2027 season
excerpt:
MP Motorsport have announced the signing of Matteo De Palo for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season.

De Palo returns for a second campaign in F3 after a rookie year where he finished 24th in the Drivers’ Championship, with a best result of P4 in the Silverstone Sprint Race.

Prior to 2025, the Italian placed second in the Formula Regional European Championship, achieving four victories and 11 podiums in total.

De Palo will now return for another campaign in F3 and he is delighted to be doing so with MP, with his sights set on continuing the good form they showed at the end of the 2026 season.

“I’m really excited to join MP Motorsport for my second year in FIA F3”, said De Palo. “Especially in the second half of this season, they were among the teams to beat, finishing the year on a high with victory, so I aim to do my part in maintaining that kind of form into 2027.

“It’s a Dutch team, but with an Italian flavour on the engineering side – I like that! The team is renowned for their welcoming atmosphere, so I’m sure I will feel right at home from the start.”

MP Motorsport Team Principal Sander Dorsman added: “It’s a delight to welcome Matteo into our Formula 3 squad for 2027. Looking back on his career, having competed with him in F4 Spanish and the Formula Regional European Championship, I’m pleased that he’s on our side now, as he’s always been a fierce competitor. I’m convinced that he will put his year of F3 experience to good use to help us to continue our forward trajectory in the championship.”

title: Gabriel Gomez steps up to FIA Formula 3 with LN4 Fusion
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion has confirmed Gabriel Gomez for the 2027 campaign.

The Brazilian steps up to FIA Formula 3 after competing in the Formula Regional European Championship in 2026, finishing 14th overall.

Gomez's single-seater career began back in 2023 in Spanish F4 before racing in a full campaign in the Championship the following year.

In 2025, he secured the Formula Winter Series title taking three wins and nine podium finishes, and finished second in both the Italian and E4 Championships, with six wins and 16 podiums between the two.

Speaking about his F3 promotion, Gomez said that he was looking forward to beginning his work with the team ahead of next season.

“I’m really happy about this opportunity to join the LN4 Fusion team and race in FIA F3 next year! I’m grateful to the team, my sponsors, and everyone who has helped make this opportunity possible. I’m really looking forward to working with everyone involved in this new project, and I’m confident we can do a great job together on track!”

Chief Executive Officer of LN4 Fusion Dan Richards added: “Gabriel has shown impressive potential so far, and we look forward to working with him. He has a remarkable resume, and we see all the ingredients for a positive season together. We are in for an exciting challenge, and we will start preparing as soon as possible to maximize what we can achieve.”

title: Alessandro Giusti completes Rodin Motorsport lineup for 2027 season
excerpt:
Alessandro Giusti will race for Rodin Motorsport in FIA Formula 3 next year.

The team confirmed the Frenchman’s signing after two seasons in the Championship, completing the lineup for 2027 with the already announced Pedro Clerot and Reza Seewooruthun.

Giusti made his F3 debut back in 2025, and after two years with MP Motorsport he moves to the Rodin outfit for a third campaign.

Speaking about his move to the team, Giusti said he was eager to get started with Rodin and that he was looking forward to the 2027 campaign already.

“I’m feeling really excited to be joining Rodin Motorsport, to discover the factory, the gym and the sim, its quite impressive! I’m really happy to get the chance to drive with the team and will push forward this season.”

Rodin Motorsport’s Sporting Director, Benn Huntingford, commented: “We’re excited to have Alessandro join our F3 lineup for 2027. He’s shown strong consistency and speed across his two seasons in the championship and brings valuable experience to the team. We’re looking forward to seeing what he can achieve with Rodin next season.”

title: Rafael Câmara signs with Haas F1 Team for 2027 season
excerpt:
Haas F1 Team has announced that Rafael Câmara will race with the team in Formula 1 in 2027.

The Brazilian driver currently leads the FIA Formula 2 Drivers' Championship with three wins this season along with four further podiums and five pole positions.

Câmara also has previous experience in Formula 1 machinery with Haas, having driven for them at Testing of Previous Cars (TPC) in August, jumping in the cockpit of the VF-25 at Autódromo Internacional do Algarve in Portimao, Portugal.

Câmara said that he was excited about the opportunity and was focused on his preparations for next season.

“I’m very happy to be joining TGR Haas F1 Team as a Formula 1 driver,” he said. “It’s an important step in my career and I want to thank Gene Haas and Ayao Komatsu for the trust they have placed in me.

“I’m also very grateful to the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for their support and for everything they have contributed to my development over the years, as well as to my family for always being there throughout this journey. Now my focus is on preparing myself in the best possible way for this new challenge. There will be a lot to learn, and I’m looking forward to working closely with the team, understanding the car and continuing to develop as a driver.”

Haas Team Principal Ayao Komatsu also added: “I’m really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Câmara. “I don’t need to tell everyone about his achievements in the junior formulas, it’s been very impressive, and in his rookie season in Formula 2, the speed he’s shown in some very difficult moments, like qualifying in Monaco and Montreal – that all goes to show the potential Rafa has.

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car, he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special. We’re all excited about this opportunity and really committed as TGR Haas F1 Team to nurture this talent and provide a place where he can flourish. We want to create an environment where he’s comfortable and supported, where he can really excel in his capabilities.”

title: Van Amersfoort Racing confirms signing of Rashid Al Dhaheri for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Rashid Al Dhaheri will step up to FIA Formula 3 in 2027 with Van Amersfoort Racing.

The team confirmed that the Emirati driver will move up to F3 after finishing fourth in this year’s Formula Regional European Championship.

Al Dhaheri’s single-seater career began back in 2023 after multiple karting accolades including WSK Champions Cup and Super Master Series OKJ titles in 2021.

The Mercedes Junior Team driver competed full-time in the Italian F4 series for two seasons along with finishing fourth in the UAE F4 championship in 2024.

In 2025, he moved up to FREC and wound up eighth in the standings in what was his rookie campaign, before returning this year and improving to fourth overall.

Speaking about his step up to F3 with VAR, Al Dhaheri said he was excited to be making the jump and taking on a new challenge.

“I’m very proud to be taking the next step into FIA Formula 3 with Van Amersfoort Racing. It is an important milestone in my journey, but I know the hard work is only beginning. I’m proud to represent the UAE and the wider region at this level, and I’m looking forward to learning, improving and giving everything I have on and off the track. Every step has to be earned, and my focus now is on preparing as strongly as possible for 2027. I’m grateful to everyone who has supported me and helped make this opportunity possible.”

Brad Joyce, Team Principal for Van Amersfoort Racing, added: “We’re looking forward to welcome Rashid to Van Amersfoort Racing. He has had a very strong season in Formula Regional, with three wins and eight podiums, finishing in fourth place in the championship. He has shown his pace throughout the year and has been able to fight at the front of a very competitive field. That gives us a good starting point as he steps up to Formula 3. We’re looking forward to working with him during the post season tests and preparing for his first F3 season together.”

title: Yevan David moves to Van Amersfoort Racing for the 2027 season
excerpt:
Van Amersfoort Racing have announced the signing of Yevan David for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season.

David returns for a second campaign in F3 after a positive rookie year where he finished 18th in the Drivers’ Championship with 35 points – helped by podium in the Silverstone Sprint Race.

Prior to this season he competed in the 2025 Euroformula Open Championship and he finished second in the Standings with six wins and 14 podiums in total.

The 19-year-old is excited to be back to compete in F3 and to be doing so with VAR.

“Stepping into VAR for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season feels like the right move at the right time,” said David. “The leadership team has a clear vision, proven experience and a competitive mindset that matches how I want to operate.

“I’m excited to learn from them, contribute to that culture and test myself against the strongest field in junior single-seaters. The challenge is big, but so is the opportunity. I’m ready to work, grow and deliver everything I can throughout the 2027 season”

Van Amersfoort Racing Team Principal Brad Joyce added: “We’re pleased to welcome Yevan to Van Amersfoort Racing. He showed great potential in his first FIA Formula 3 season, with a strong second-place finish in the Silverstone Sprint Race.

“Joining the VAR team will give him a new environment for his second year, and our aim is to turn that experience into great results. We’re looking forward to getting to know him and working with him during the post-season test. This will be a good opportunity to prepare for the 2027 season.”

title: A tribute to his father and an F1 Icon: Fernando Barrichello on his Special Helmet Design
excerpt:
Fernando Barrichello recently spoke about his special tribute helmet to his father Rubens Barrichello

Fernando Barrichello had a new look for the final rounds of the season, as he raced with an eye-catching new helmet.

Blending his own design with his father, Rubens, the Brazilian paid tribute to the multi-time Formula 1 race winner. We caught up with him to talk through it all, including the emotional moment he did the big reveal.

“It's a big dream come true for me to be honest. Obviously watching my dad growing up who had such an iconic design that he had always worn since he was a little kid.

“I always wanted to create a place for myself. But I always knew that at some point I really wanted to honour him and pay respect to everything that he's done. I had been thinking about it for a long time, thinking of how I exactly I wanted to do that.

“His helmet is the way it's supposed to be. You can see that the bottom is his helmet and mine is sort of on top.

Barrichello ran the helmet at the final two rounds of the season in Monza and Madrid

“What I wanted to show is that his helmet has always been on the bottom, and mine is just a layer over everything.

“Obviously, everything that I know and believe in this sport, especially the passion that I have for it, has come from him. So it's an honour to be able to do this but just to show that he's always been under everything.

LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of James Egozi for the 2027 season

Kanato Le returns with Hitech for the 2027 Formula 3 season

“I did a big surprise. He had no idea and he didn't know that this was going to happen, and so when we got together, I showed it to him.

“It was a very emotional one to be honest. I got it on video, so it was really nice. It was really nice to see how surprised he was and just how happy he was. Obviously telling him this was really nice, so it was a special one.

“It's pretty cool in that sense. To be honest, like I said, I've always wanted to do it, but the window never really came about too much.

The Brazilian talked through the right process and why it was the right time to design the helmet

“Arai sent me a new helmet mid-season so we could have a second one here, and it was right around the time where he drove his Ferrari at the Red Bull Ring. I saw it there and everything was sort of aligning for it to happen.

“I felt like that was a really good opportunity, and then it was, to be honest, a good couple of weeks with the people from Infinity.

TRIDENT signs Sebastian Wheldon for 2027 campaign

Woohyun Shin returns with Hitech for 2027 season

“We were thinking and doing a bunch of different designs. We thought of many different things and I wanted it to be as special as possible. So we really thought about every single design possible.

“I'm a bit of a pain, so I do have to apologise to them, but the result came out exactly like I wanted it.

“I've jumped in the car with it for the first time to do radio checks, and there's a little mirror on top of the steering wheel, and I can see myself. It was really special.”

title: LN4 Fusion confirm the signing of James Egozi for the 2027 season
excerpt:
LN4 Fusion have confirmed their first driver signing for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season, with James Egozi joining the team for the upcoming campaign.

Egozi joins the team after a stellar 2026 season, as he started the year finishing second in the Eurocup-3 Spanish Winter Championship.

The American followed that up by winning this year’s Eurocup-3 title with two rounds to spare, having won eight races and achieved 12 podiums in total.

Egozi will now take the next step in his career by graduating to Formula 3, and he spoke of his delight at getting to join the newly formed team.

"I am truly grateful to the entire Team for giving me the opportunity to join such an exciting project with LN4 Fusion,” said Egozi. “I'm ready to continue my development as a driver, and I am hungrier than ever for the 2027 FIA F3 season."

LN4 Fusion Chief Executive Officer Dan Richards added: "We are really delighted to have James on board. He has always been a very interesting prospect, and he made a remarkable breakthrough this year by dominating the Eurocup-3 championship. His results speak for themselves and we look forward to building on that form as we establish ourselves in the FIA Formula 3 Championship."

title: Kanato Le returns with Hitech for the 2027 Formula 3 season
excerpt:
Hitech have confirmed the signing of Kanato Le for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season, completing their line-up for next season.

Le returns for a second season in F3 after a finishing 20th in the Drivers’ Standings with 30 points – helped by a podium finish in the Budapest Sprint.

The Japanese driver and Hitech have a history together having firstly competed in a full season together in 2023, and Le finished seventh in the British F4 Championship with two wins.

They reunited earlier this year in the Formula Regional Oceania Trophy, and Le ended up sixth in the Standings with one victory and six podiums in total.

This announcement means the British team’s driver lineup for the upcoming campaign is complete following the announcements of Keanu Al Ahzari and Woohyun Shin.

Le and Hitech will now compete together in Formula 3 in 2027, and at the announcement, he expressed how happy he was to be racing with the team.

“I am really looking forward to racing with Hitech in FIA Formula 3 for the 2027 season,” said Le. “It’s a team I know very well after racing with them in British F4 and CTFROC, and I am excited to be part of the team again.

“I am confident that we will have a strong season together. I would also like to thank everyone for the continued support.”

Hitech Team Manager Paul Bellringer also added: “We’re delighted to welcome Kanato back to Hitech and complete our FIA Formula 3 line-up for 2027.

“Kanato is a driver we know very well, having worked with him at different stages of his career. He’s always had good natural speed and racecraft, and it’s been rewarding to see him gain experience and develop over the last few seasons.

“His first year in FIA Formula 3 has given him a much better understanding of the demands of the championship, and he showed what he is capable of with his podium in Hungary and strong qualifying performance at Monza.

“It was also great to have him back racing with us at Brands Hatch recently. He settled straight back in and delivered another podium, which says a lot about his ability to adapt and get up to speed.

“With Kanato confirmed, our 2027 driver line-up is now complete. We have a good combination of talent and experience, and we're looking forward to getting to work with all three drivers as we prepare for next season.”

title: TRIDENT signs Sebastian Wheldon for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Sebastian Wheldon will step up to FIA Formula 3 in 2027 with TRIDENT.

The Italian team confirmed that the American will race with the Milanese outfit next season after finishing this year’s Formula Regional European Championship campaign in second.

Prior to that, Wheldon debuted in single-seater racing back in 2023, winning the Skip Barber Formula Race Series with six wins.

He moved onto the YACademy Winter Series in 2024, finishing second before finishing the USF Juniors series third overall.

In 2025, he secured seven wins across the F4 Middle East, E4 and Italian F4 Championships, finishing third overall in the latter with six victories, three poles and nine podiums overall.

Speaking about his signing with TRIDENT in F3, Wheldon says that he was excited about the next step in his career.

“I'm very happy to be competing in the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship with TRIDENT Motorsport. There's a lot of pressure, as I'll be racing for one of the most successful teams in the category. However, I love a challenge and will give my all to learn quickly and achieve good results. I'm extremely grateful to TWG Motorsports and Andretti Global for their support. I can't wait for next season to begin. Let's go!”

TRIDENT Team Manager Giacomo Ricci added: “We are delighted to announce our agreement with Sebastian Wheldon for the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship season. Sebastian is a driver who has demonstrated consistent growth throughout his career, distinguishing himself both in the United States and Europe. His 2026 Formula Regional season, which he finished in second place, confirmed his talent and ability to compete at the highest level. We are confident that Trident Motorsport represents the ideal environment to support him in the next step of his promising career.”

title: Woohyun Shin returns with Hitech for 2027 season
excerpt:
Hitech has confirmed that Woohyun Shin will race with the team in 2027. The South Korean driver competed with the British outfit in 2026 and will return for what will be his second full season in FIA Formula 3.

Prior to F3, Shin secured P3 in the Euroformula Open Championship in 2025, improving on the fifth place he earned in the series the year prior.

He also finished fourth in the 2024 Formula Regional Oceania Championship.

Speaking about his re-signing with Hitech, Shin said he was happy to be back with the team once again.

“There are particular aspects to the FIA Formula 3 championship that make it very competitive and challenging. I felt that there would be more to come from me by staying another year and further working on those areas in a familiar environment.

“I want to thank the team for believing in me and making it possible to continue our journey together.”

Hitech F3 Team Manager Paul Bellringer added: “We’re pleased to continue our relationship with Michael into the 2027 FIA Formula 3 season. This year has been an important learning process for him, returning to FIA F3 for a full campaign after his previous experience in the championship.

“Michael has had to learn a lot throughout the season, from the car and tyres to the level of competition and the demands of racing at this level. Having that experience behind him will be valuable heading into his second year.

“We know Michael well from his previous time with Hitech, and we believe there is a lot more to come from him. Continuity is important in Formula 3, and giving him another season with the team will allow us to build on the work we have already done together.

“We’re looking forward to seeing Michael take the next step in 2027 and continuing his development with Hitech.”

title: Enzo Deligny remains with Van Amersfoort Racing for 2027 season
excerpt:
Van Amersfoort Racing has confirmed that Enzo Deligny will remain with the team for his second FIA Formula 3 campaign in 2027.

Deligny made his debut this year, racing with VAR and finishing the season 16th in the Drivers' Championship, earning a podium on debut in Melbourne.

The Frenchman secured a further two top five finishes and seven top 10 results across the year.

Speaking about his re-signing with Van Amersfoort, Deligny said that he was pleased to be returning with the team.

“I'm really happy to be continuing with VAR for 2027. After joining the team late this season, I immediately felt very comfortable and we’ve built a strong relationship. I’m really looking forward to starting next year together and showing what we can achieve. Having stability by staying with this great team will help me perform next year. I can't wait.”

VAR Team Principal Brad Joyce added: “We’re pleased to continue our collaboration with Enzo for another season. He made a very strong start to his FIA Formula 3 career in Melbourne, finishing second in the Sprint Race on his debut weekend. He has now gained a full year of experience in the championship, and working with him throughout the season has given us the opportunity to see his talent up close. That experience and continuity are important as we look to build on what we started in 2026 and push for stronger results in 2027.”

title: Keanu Al Azhari joins Hitech for 2027 campaign
excerpt:
Hitech has announced that Keanu Al Azhari will step up to FIA Formula 3 with the team next season.

The 18-year-old joins the Championship after competing with Hitech across multiple seasons. In 2025 in GB3, the combination brought a race win, six podiums and three pole positions.

This year, he has raced with Hitech in the Eurocup-3 Spanish Winter Championship and Eurocup-3. In the former, Al Azhari earned two wins and seven podiums to win the title. In Eurocup-3, the Emirati driver currently sits third in the standings with two rounds to go with a race win to his name.

Al Alzhari said that he was proud to be representing the UAE and was very excited about his graduation to F3 with the Hitech team.

“I am proud and honoured to continue my journey with my family at Hitech as we step up together into the 2027 FIA Formula 3 Championship.

“To become the first driver from the UAE to compete in FIA Formula 3 is a milestone I carry with immense pride. Representing my nation at this level is the greatest honour, and I'm humbled by the support of the UAE behind me.

“I hope this journey inspires the next generation of drivers across our region to dream without limits.”

Paul Bellringer, Hitech’s FIA F3 Team Manager added: “It’s great to see Keanu making the step into FIA Formula 3 with us. We’ve worked closely with him over the last two seasons and have seen first-hand how much he has developed in that time.

“He has shown his speed with race wins and podiums, but one of his real strengths is his ability to race his way through the field. Even when a weekend hasn’t gone to plan or conditions are difficult, he finds a way to move forward and put himself in contention. That ability to make something out of challenging situations will serve him well in Formula 3.

“There’s something particularly rewarding about seeing a driver progress through the different levels of Hitech and reach F3 with us. Keanu knows how we work, we know what he is capable of, and we’re looking forward to continuing that progression together in 2027.”

title: FIA Formula 3 unveils 2027 calendar
excerpt:
The FIA Formula 3 Championship has announced its 2027 calendar, featuring 10 rounds across four continents and three exciting new venues: Jeddah, Montreal and Istanbul.

The campaign will bring Formula 3 to North America for the first time, while expanding further the Championship’s international footprint.

The season will begin in March with two back-to-back events. Sakhir, Bahrain, will host the opening round alongside Formula 1 and Formula 2 before the field travels to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, where the 30 F3 cars will take on the fast and demanding Jeddah Corniche Circuit for the very first time.

Melbourne, Australia, will follow in April, before Formula 3 makes its historic North American debut in May. Montreal will host Round 4, offering the drivers another new challenge at the Circuit Gilles-Villeneuve.

The Championship will return to the streets of Monaco, in June for two back-to-back rounds will then take place in July, beginning at Silverstone, Great Britain, and followed by Spielberg, Austria.

After the summer break, the season will resume with another double-header. The teams and drivers will first compete at Monza, Italy, before travelling to Madrid, Spain.

Finally, the 2027 campaign will conclude at Istanbul, Türkiye, the third new venue on the calendar. Formula 3’s first visit to Istanbul Park will provide a demanding and fitting finale to a season of unprecedented geographical reach.

Mohammed Ben Sulayem, FIA President said: ““Formula 3 is where many drivers begin to prove themselves on the international stage, and the 2027 calendar will give them an exceptional range of challenges where they can develop their skills. Racing in North America for the first time is an important milestone for the Championship, while the additions of Jeddah and Istanbul will test our drivers across demanding circuits.

“Providing young talent with these experiences is fundamental to building the future of our sport, and I look forward to watching this next generation rise to the challenge throughout the 2027 season.”

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1 said: "We have seen great racing in Formula 3 in 2026, including an incredible fight for the title, which ultimately went to the first ever American driver to win the Championship, and the 2027 season is set to build on that momentum with another exciting generation of young talent coming through the motorsport pyramid. Racing alongside Formula 1 is a unique opportunity for these drivers to develop their skills, showcase their potential and prepare themselves for the demands of the highest level of our sport. The 2027 calendar marks an exciting step for Formula 3, with the Championship visiting four continents and introducing new venues that will provide fresh challenges for drivers and teams alike. I would like to thank the FIA President and their entire team, Bruno Michel and his team, as well as our promoters, partners, officials, marshals and volunteers, whose dedication and commitment make the Championship possible. Formula 3 continues to play a vital role in developing the stars of tomorrow, and I look forward to another outstanding season of racing in 2027."

Bruno Michel, FIA Formula 3 CEO said: “The 2027 FIA Formula 3 calendar is groundbreaking, with three new venues that represent a formidable challenge for the teams and the drivers. It will be very exciting to see the F3 cars at the Jeddah Corniche Circuit, and I’m extremely pleased to bring F3 to North America for the very first time thanks to the addition of Montreal to the calendar. Istanbul Park will host the season finale, another new challenge next season. Just like for F2, we will be covering freight costs so that the territorial expansion of the calendar does not financially impact our teams.”
